newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Wooltru year figures seen strong.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Wooltru year figures seen strong.

text.p: Analysts are bullish about year-end results of retail group Wooltru Ltd on good growth in operations but slower consumer spending due to high interest rates may hold back the firm's performance.
Analysts forecast earnings per share in the year to June 30, 1997, to rise to between 114 cents and 120 cents from last year's 109.1 cents with the consensus at 117 cents.
The dividend is forecast at 45 to 54 cents with consensus at 47 cents compared to last year's 42 cents.
Wooltru will report financial results on Thursday, August 21.
"I expect them to be substantially up on last year," said one analyst.

"They took a big knock in the second half of the previous year from Massmart, which has not been repeated, while Woolworths WLWR.CN textiles have had a better year and the volume of food sales has been well up," he said.

"Some people have been downgrading it because of Truworths' problems with credit but Woolworths is a completely different thing. The fact that they have only started their sales now, instead of mid-July, shows that there was nothing left to sell."
But several analysts said that while they expected good results, they were concerned about the effect of slower retail sales trends on the group.
"Interest rates really started to bite in the second half of the year and I suspect that market conditions have been tougher," said one analyst.
He added that Woolworths' textiles had done exceptionally well and it had been offered rare praise by retailer Stuttafords, which had reported that it had lost a lot of market share to Woolworths.
"They have got it right after some mistakes the previous year," he said.
The Australian Sports Girl outlets had misread fashions and could pull earnings down somewhat, but analysts remained upbeat about the group as a whole.
One analyst was particular excited about speculation that Wooltru planned to start its own in-house bank along United Kingdom's Marks & Spencer Plc lines, which would boost margins.

This follows Woolworths' decision to buy back its private-label credit card debtors' book from Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd and analysts said the book now had a better quality. Credit cards helped boost sales by about 30 percent.
Wooltru's plans to separately list Woolworths and Truworths were reported to be still on track although Truworths had been delayed until next year.

Woolworths' recent expansion of its holdings in Australia's Country Road Ltd was seen as positive although the group had distribution problems and, like many other retailers worldwide, had misread fashion trends.
